description_en: GNOME gnome-keyring 3.4.0 through 3.4.1, when gpg-cache-method is set to "idle" or "timeout," does not properly limit the amount of time a passphrase is cached, which allows attackers to have an unspecified impact via unknown attack vectors.

GNOME Keyring through 3.28.2 allows local users to retrieve login credentials via a Secret Service API call and the D-Bus interface if the keyring is unlocked, a similar issue to CVE-2008-7320. One perspective is that this occurs because available D-Bus protection mechanisms (involving the busconfig and policy XML elements) are not used. NOTE: the vendor disputes this because, according to the security model, untrusted applications must not be allowed to access the user's session bus socket.

A flaw was found in all released versions of m2crypto, where they are vulnerable to Bleichenbacher timing attacks in the RSA decryption API via the timed processing of valid PKCS#1 v1.5 Ciphertext. The highest threat from this vulnerability is to confidentiality.

An Improper Handling of Exceptional Conditions vulnerability in packet processing of Juniper Networks Junos OS on MX Series with MPC10/MPC11/LC9600 line cards, EX9200 with EX9200-15C lines cards, MX304 devices, and Juniper Networks Junos OS Evolved on PTX Series, allows an attacker sending malformed DHCP packets to cause ingress packet processing to stop, leading to a Denial of Service (DoS).  Continued receipt and processing of these packets will create a sustained Denial of Service (DoS) condition.

This issue only occurs if DHCP snooping is enabled. See configuration below.

This issue can be detected using following commands. Their output will display the interface status going down:


user@device>show interfaces <if--x/x/x>
user@device>show log messages | match <if--x/x/x>
user@device>show log messages ==> will display the "[Error] Wedge-Detect : Host Loopback Wedge Detected: PFE: no," logs.

This issue affects:
Junos OS on 

MX Series 

with MPC10/MPC11/LC9600 line cards, EX9200 with EX9200-15C line cards, and MX304: 


  *  All versions before 21.2R3-S7, 
  *  from 21.4 before 21.4R3-S6, 
  *  from 22.2 before 22.2R3-S3, 
  *  all versions of 22.3,
  *  from 22.4 before 22.4R3, 
  *  from 23.2 before 23.2R2; 



Junos OS Evolved on PTX Series: 
  *  from 19.3R1-EVO before 21.2R3-S8-EVO,

  *  from 21.4-EVO before 21.4R3-S7-EVO, 
  *  from 22.1-EVO before 22.1R3-S6-EVO, 
  *  from 22.2-EVO before 22.2R3-S5-EVO, 
  *  from 22.3-EVO before 22.3R3-S3-EVO, 
  *  from 22.4-EVO before 22.4R3-S1-EVO, 
  *  from 23.2-EVO before 23.2R2-S2-EVO, 
  *  from 23.4-EVO before 23.4R2-EVO.



Junos OS Evolved releases prior to 19.3R1-EVO are unaffected by this vulnerability

A NULL Pointer Dereference vulnerability in the Packet Forwarding Engine (pfe) of Juniper Networks Junos OS allows a local, low-privileged attacker to cause a Denial-of-Service (DoS).

When a specific command is executed, the pfe crashes. This will cause traffic forwarding to be interrupted until the system self-recovers. Repeated execution will create a sustained DoS condition.

 This issue only affects MX Series devices with Line cards MPC1-MPC9.
This issue affects:
Junos OS on MX Series: 


  *  All versions before 21.4R3-S9, 
  *  from 22.2 before 22.2R3-S5, 
  *  from 22.3 before 22.3R3-S4, 
  *  from 22.4 before 22.4R3-S2, 
  *  from 23.2 before 23.2R2-S1, 
  *  from 23.4 before 23.4R2.

Improper encoding or escaping of output vulnerability in the system plugin daemon in Synology BeeStation OS (BSM) before 1.1-65374 and Synology DiskStation Manager (DSM) before 7.2-64570-4, 7.2.1-69057-6 and 7.2.2-72806-1 allows remote attackers to execute arbitrary code via unspecified vectors.

urllib3 is a user-friendly HTTP client library for Python. Starting in version 2.2.0 and prior to 2.5.0, urllib3 does not control redirects in browsers and Node.js. urllib3 supports being used in a Pyodide runtime utilizing the JavaScript Fetch API or falling back on XMLHttpRequest. This means Python libraries can be used to make HTTP requests from a browser or Node.js. Additionally, urllib3 provides a mechanism to control redirects, but the retries and redirect parameters are ignored with Pyodide; the runtime itself determines redirect behavior. This issue has been patched in version 2.5.0.
OPEXUS eComplaint before version 9.0.45.0 allows an attacker to visit the 'DocumentOpen.aspx' endpoint, iterate through predictable values of 'chargeNumber', and download any uploaded files.

It was possible to improperly access the parent directory of an os.Root by opening a filename ending in "../". For example, Root.Open("../") would open the parent directory of the Root. This escape only permits opening the parent directory itself, not ancestors of the parent or files contained within the parent.

Use of a Broken or Risky Cryptographic Algorithm vulnerability in rustdesk-server-pro RustDesk Server Pro rustdesk-server-pro on Windows, MacOS, Linux (Config string generation, web console export modules) allows Retrieve Embedded Sensitive Data. This vulnerability is associated with program routines Config export/generation routines.

This issue affects RustDesk Server Pro: through 1.7.5. NOTE: the Supplier's position is that this is not a vulnerability.

Improperly Controlled Modification of Object Prototype Attributes ('Prototype Pollution'), Use of Password Hash With Insufficient Computational Effort vulnerability in rustdesk-client RustDesk Client rustdesk, hbb_common on Windows, MacOS, Linux (Password security module, config encryption, machine UID modules) allows Retrieve Embedded Sensitive Data. This vulnerability is associated with program files hbb_common/src/password_security.Rs, hbb_common/src/config.Rs, hbb_common/src/lib.Rs (get_uuid), machine-uid/src/lib.Rs and program routines symmetric_crypt(), encrypt_str_or_original(), decrypt_str_or_original(), get_uuid(), get_machine_id().

This issue affects RustDesk Client: through 1.4.5. NOTE: some third parties have indicated that these details do not align with the Supplier's statements.

A vulnerability in rustdesk-client RustDesk Client rustdesk-client on Windows, MacOS, Linux, iOS, Android, WebClient (Strategy sync, HTTP API client, config options engine modules) allows Application API Message Manipulation via Man-in-the-Middle.

 This vulnerability is associated with program files src/hbbs_http/sync.Rs, hbb_common/src/config.Rs and program routines Strategy merge loop in sync.Rs, Config::set_options().



This issue affects RustDesk Client: through 1.4.8. NOTE: some third parties have indicated that these details do not align with the Supplier's statements.

Cross-Site Request Forgery (CSRF) vulnerability in rustdesk-client RustDesk Client rustdesk-client on Windows, MacOS, Linux, iOS, Android (Flutter URI scheme handler, FFI bridge modules) allows Privilege Escalation. This vulnerability is associated with program files flutter/lib/common.Dart, src/flutter_ffi.Rs and program routines URI handler for rustdesk://password/, bind.MainSetPermanentPassword().

This issue affects RustDesk Client: through 1.4.5. NOTE: some third parties have indicated that these details do not align with the Supplier's statements.

Cleartext Transmission of Sensitive Information, Insufficiently Protected Credentials vulnerability in rustdesk-client RustDesk Client rustdesk-client on Windows, MacOS, Linux, iOS, Android (Address book sync, Heartbeat sync loop modules) allows Sniffing Attacks.

The client places the preset address-book password verbatim into the heartbeat sync JSON body (src/hbbs_http/sync.rs). Over an intact HTTPS session it is not exposed in transit, but it is a reusable shared secret rather than a zero-knowledge proof, so it is recovered by any party that becomes the API endpoint - under the re-homed/rogue API server (CVE-2026-30797) - and the leaked credential then authorizes the server-side address book.

This vulnerability is associated with program files src/hbbs_http/sync.rs and program routines heartbeat sync body builder (emits preset-address-book-password).

This issue affects RustDesk Client: through 1.4.8. NOTE: some third parties have indicated that these details do not align with the Supplier's statements.

Missing Authorization vulnerability in rustdesk-client RustDesk Client rustdesk-client on Windows, MacOS, Linux, iOS, Android (Flutter URI scheme handler, config import modules) allows Application API Message Manipulation via Man-in-the-Middle. This vulnerability is associated with program files flutter/lib/common.Dart and program routines importConfig() via URI handler.

This issue affects RustDesk Client: through 1.4.5. NOTE: some third parties have indicated that these details do not align with the Supplier's statements.

Insufficient Verification of Data Authenticity, Improper Handling of Exceptional Conditions vulnerability in rustdesk-client RustDesk Client rustdesk-client on Windows, MacOS, Linux, iOS, Android (Heartbeat sync loop, strategy processing modules) allows Protocol Manipulation.

 This vulnerability is associated with program files src/hbbs_http/sync.Rs and program routines stop-service handler in heartbeat loop.



This issue affects RustDesk Client: through 1.4.8. NOTE: the Supplier's position is that this is not a vulnerability.

OPEXUS eComplaint and eCASE before 10.2.0.0 do not correctly sanitize the contents of first and last name fields in a user profile. An authenticated attacker can inject parts of an XSS payload in their first and last name fields. The payload is executed when the user's full name is rendered. The attacker can run script in the context of a victim's session.

cryptography is a package designed to expose cryptographic primitives and recipes to Python developers. Prior to version 46.0.6, DNS name constraints were only validated against SANs within child certificates, and not the "peer name" presented during each validation. Consequently, cryptography would allow a peer named bar.example.com to validate against a wildcard leaf certificate for *.example.com, even if the leaf's parent certificate (or upwards) contained an excluded subtree constraint for bar.example.com. This issue has been patched in version 46.0.6.
LiteLLM through 2026-04-08 allows remote attackers to execute arbitrary code via bytecode rewriting at the /guardrails/test_custom_code URI.

A flaw was found in the X.Org X server. This out-of-bounds read vulnerability in the XKB geometry processing, specifically within the `CheckSetGeom()` and `XkbAddGeomKeyAlias` functions, allows an attacker to read uninitialized or out-of-bounds memory. An attacker with a connection to the X11 server, either locally or remotely, can exploit this without user interaction. This could lead to the disclosure of memory contents or cause a denial of service by crashing the server.

A flaw was found in the X.Org X server. This vulnerability, an out-of-bounds read, affects the XKB (X Keyboard Extension) modifier map handling. An attacker with access to the X11 server can exploit this by sending a malformed request, which causes the server to read beyond its intended memory boundaries. This can lead to the exposure of sensitive information or cause the server to crash, resulting in a denial of service.

Vim is an open source, command line text editor. Prior to 9.2.0670, get_text_props() in src/textprop.c reads a uint16 property count stored inline after a line's text and returns it as the number of 32-byte textprop_T entries that follow. The only check is a floor that guarantees room for a single entry; the count is never checked against the amount of data actually present. A line that declares a large count while carrying little data causes consumers to read far past the end of the line buffer. Such a line can be delivered through a crafted undo file, leading to a crash. This vulnerability is fixed in 9.2.0670.
Improper access control in Windows Server allows an authorized attacker to elevate privileges locally.

A vulnerability exists in NGINX Plus and NGINX Open Source when a map directive uses regex matching and a string expression references the map's regex capture variables before referencing the map output variable. Alternatively, the same result could be achieved by using a non-cacheable variable in a string expression under certain conditions. An unauthenticated attacker along with conditions beyond their control can exploit this vulnerability by sending crafted HTTP requests. This may cause a heap buffer overflow in the NGINX worker process leading to a restart. Additionally, attackers can execute code on systems with Address Space Layout Randomization (ASLR) disabled or when the attacker can bypass ASLR.

Impact:
This vulnerability may allow remote attackers to cause a denial-of-service (DoS) on the NGINX system or to possibly trigger a code execution. There is no control plane exposure; this is a data plane issue only.




 Note: Software versions which have reached End of Technical Support (EoTS) are not evaluated.

NGINX Plus and NGINX Open Source have a vulnerability in the ngx_http_ssi_module module. This vulnerability may exist when the Server-Side Includes (SSI), proxy_pass, and proxy_buffering off directives are configured. With this configuration, an unauthenticated attacker with man-in-the-middle (MITM) ability to control responses from an upstream server may be able to cause a use-after-free in the NGINX worker process. This issue may lead to limited modification of memory or a restart of the NGINX worker process.

Impact:
This vulnerability may allow remote attackers to have limited control to modify memory contents or restart the NGINX worker process. There is no control plane exposure; this is a data plane issue only.

Note: Software versions which have reached End of Technical Support (EoTS) are not evaluated.

NGINX Plus and NGINX Open Source have a vulnerability in the ngx_http_slice_module module. When the slice directive and unnamed regex captures are configured or when a background cache update happens, unauthenticated attackers can send requests that may cause uninitialized memory access in the NGINX worker process, leading to limited disclosure of memory or a restart.

Impact:
This vulnerability may allow remote, unauthenticated attackers to have limited control to disclose memory contents or restart the NGINX worker process. There is no control plane exposure; this is a data plane issue only.
Note: The ngx_http_slice_module module is not enabled by default; it's enabled with the --with-http_slice_module configuration parameter.

Note: Software versions which have reached End of Technical Support (EoTS) are not evaluated.

MLflow is an open source AI engineering platform for agents, large language models, and machine learning models. Starting in 3.3.0 and prior to 3.15.0, the POST /api/2.0/mlflow/webhooks/{id}/test endpoint (accessible without credentials when server authentication is not enabled) calls _validate_webhook_url() in mlflow/utils/validation.py only for the original URL while mlflow/webhooks/delivery.py follows redirects and re-resolves the hostname without pinning the validated address, allowing attackers to reach internal or cloud metadata services and receive response_status and response_body. The unauthenticated attack scenario described here applies to deployments without authentication. With MLflow’s built-in basic authentication enabled, requests to this endpoint require valid credentials; this issue does not itself bypass authentication. This issue is fixed in version 3.15.0.
Improper access control in Microsoft Office SharePoint allows an authorized attacker to execute code over a network.
Improper access control in Microsoft Office SharePoint allows an authorized attacker to execute code over a network.
Heap-based buffer overflow in Microsoft Office allows an unauthorized attacker to execute code over a network.
Incorrect authorization in Azure Machine Learning allows an unauthorized attacker to disclose information over a network.

An unauthenticated Remote Code Execution vulnerability was found in the survey passthrough routing and Data Import processing logic, in which a malicious user could potentially exploit it by manipulating HTTP requests to access an unintended controller route from a public survey context and by supplying a crafted file-path/stream parameter during import handling. If successfully exploited, this could allow the attacker to remotely execute arbitrary code on the REDCap server. The attacker does not have to be authenticated in order to exploit this, but exploitation requires knowledge of a valid public survey hash. This vulnerability exists in REDCap 13.3.0 and higher.

A command injection flaw was found in rpm. Installing or rebuilding a source RPM whose source or spec file basenames contain a %() macro construct causes rpm to execute an attacker-controlled shell command via popen() while relocating the source file list. This allows arbitrary command execution as the invoking (typically non-root) user, simply by installing, rebuilding, or otherwise processing an untrusted .src.rpm.

A heap-based buffer overflow flaw was found in rpm. Parsing a symlink entry in an untrusted RPM package whose declared RPMTAG_LONGFILESIZES value is 0xFFFFFFFFFFFFFFFF causes an integer overflow in iterReadArchiveNext() that shrinks a buffer allocation to one byte, after which the payload's independently-controlled cpio filesize field is used to write attacker-controlled data past the end of that allocation. This is reachable via rpm2cpio, rpm2archive, and rpm -qlvp on an  untrusted package.

virtualenv is a tool for creating isolated virtual python environments. Prior to 21.7.12, download_wheel() accepts pip and setuptools seed wheels fetched for periodic updates or the --download option without checking their bytes against an authoritative digest equivalent to the embedded wheels' BUNDLE_SHA256 verification. A compromised index, stale mirror, or intercepted TLS connection can substitute a different wheel under the requested distribution, version, and filename, after which virtualenv caches and seeds the attacker-controlled wheel into subsequently created environments. The verification applies to the default PyPI path and is intentionally skipped when PIP_INDEX_URL, PIP_EXTRA_INDEX_URL, or PIP_INDEX configures a custom index that may legitimately publish rebuilt wheels. This issue is fixed in version 21.7.12.

virtualenv is a tool for creating isolated virtual python environments. Prior to 21.7.12, BatchActivator.quote() returns prompt text unchanged before activate.bat inserts it into a cmd.exe set "VAR=value" statement. An attacker who influences --prompt, VIRTUALENV_PROMPT, or the corresponding configuration value can include a double quote that closes the assignment and leaves following cmd.exe operators as executable syntax. When a user activates the generated Windows environment, the injected commands run with that user's privileges. This issue is fixed in version 21.7.12.

virtualenv is a tool for creating isolated virtual python environments. Prior to 21.7.11, PyEnvCfg.write() writes prompt values verbatim to the line-oriented pyvenv.cfg format while PyEnvCfg._read_values() parses the file with str.splitlines() and accepts the last value for duplicate keys. An attacker who influences --prompt, VIRTUALENV_PROMPT, or configuration input can insert a recognized line boundary and additional keys, including home, causing consumers to use an attacker-selected base interpreter or corrupted environment metadata. The security impact requires prompt input from outside the operator's trust boundary; directly supplied prompt content primarily corrupts the operator's own environment. This issue is fixed in version 21.7.11.

A heap-based buffer overflow flaw was found in rpm. RPMTAG_FILESIGNATURES in a crafted, unsigned RPM package's main header is declared with the wrong header type, causing hex2binv() to allocate a one-byte buffer and then write the tag's attacker-controlled, hex-decoded content — of attacker-chosen length — past the end of that allocation. This is reachable via rpm2cpio, rpm2archive, and rpm -qlvp on an untrusted package.

Improper authentication in ASP.NET Core allows an unauthorized attacker to elevate privileges over a network.

A vulnerability exists in NGINX Plus and NGINX Open Source when a location is configured that uses the alias directive together with rewrite and a set or return directive referencing the $request_filename variable. Alternatively, the same result could be achieved when the $request_filename variable is used in an access log format directive. An unauthenticated attacker along with conditions beyond their control can exploit this vulnerability by sending crafted HTTP requests. This may cause a heap buffer overflow in the NGINX worker process leading to a restart. Additionally, attackers can execute code on systems with Address Space Layout Randomization (ASLR) disabled or when the attacker can bypass ASLR.

Impact:
This vulnerability may allow remote attackers to cause a denial-of-service (DoS) on the NGINX system or to possibly trigger a code execution. There is no control plane exposure; this is a data plane issue only.




Note: Software versions which have reached End of Technical Support (EoTS) are not evaluated.

NGINX Plus and NGINX Open Source have a vulnerability in the ngx_http_core_module module. When asynchronous file I/O (AIO) is enabled in certain configurations, processing a Server Side Includes (SSI) page containing “include virtual” commands may trigger a Use-After-Free (UAF) in the NGINX worker process. This may cause memory corruption or a worker process crash. Additionally, attackers can execute code on systems with Address Space Layout Randomization (ASLR) disabled or when the attacker can bypass ASLR.

Impact:
This vulnerability may allow remote attackers to cause a denial-of-service (DoS) on the NGINX system, corrupt its memory, or possibly trigger code execution. There is no control plane exposure; this is a data plane issue only.




Note: Software versions which have reached End of Technical Support (EoTS) are not evaluated.

Description
When NGINX Plus or NGINX Open Source is configured with ssl_session_cache 

shared:name:size

without an explicit ssl_session_ticket_key file directives to automatically rotate SSL session ticket keys, a remote unauthenticated attacker is able to forge client SSL sessions 

in a non-deterministic manner that is beyond the attacker's control. An attacker could leverage this vulnerability to bypass verification of client certificates.

Impact


This vulnerability can lead to the exposure of resources or functionality to unintended actors, possibly providing attackers with access to sensitive information. There is no control plane exposure; this is a data plane issue only.






Note: Software versions which have reached End of Technical Support (EoTS) are not evaluated.

Vulnerability in the Oracle Communications Unified Inventory Management product of Oracle Communications (component: Security).  Supported versions that are affected are 7.5.0, 7.5.1, 7.6.0, 7.7.0, 7.8.0 and 8.0.1. Difficult to exploit vulnerability allows low privileged attacker with network access via HTTP to compromise Oracle Communications Unified Inventory Management.  Successful attacks of this vulnerability can result in takeover of Oracle Communications Unified Inventory Management. CVSS 3.1 Base Score 7.5 (Confidentiality, Integrity and Availability impacts).  CVSS Vector: (CVSS:3.1/AV:N/AC:H/PR:L/UI:N/S:U/C:H/I:H/A:H).

Vulnerability in the MySQL Server, MySQL Cluster product of Oracle MySQL (component: Server: Optimizer).  Supported versions that are affected are MySQL Server: 8.4.0-8.4.12, 9.7.0-9.7.3, 26.7.0-26.7.1; MySQL Cluster: 8.0.0-8.0.49, 8.4.0-8.4.12, 9.7.0-9.7.3 and  26.7.0-26.7.1. OpenMage magento-lts before 20.2.0 contains a stored cross-site scripting vulnerability because the TinyMCE WYSIWYG editor fails to filter scripts in specially crafted HTML tags. Attackers can inject an img element with a malicious onmouseover attribute to execute scripts in the browsers of users viewing the rendered content.

EdgeChat 2.5.0 through 2.21.0 contains a cross-site scripting vulnerability that allows invited users to inject HTML through unescaped usernames in the Vditor @-mention autocomplete. Attackers can register with a username containing an img onerror payload that executes when mentioned, stealing the localStorage session token to take over victim accounts.

HomeBox is a home inventory and organization system. Prior to 0.27.0, the unauthenticated GET /swagger/doc.json endpoint copies the client-supplied X-Forwarded-Host header into the OpenAPI host field without requiring a trusted proxy or validating the value. An attacker can therefore make the served OpenAPI document direct Swagger UI Try it out requests to an attacker-controlled host. When a shared cache or CDN stores and serves that poisoned document to an authenticated user, Swagger UI sends the user's API requests and bearer token to the attacker, enabling disclosure and modification of the user's HomeBox data. Without a shared cache, the attacker can affect only the attacker's own response. This issue is fixed in version 0.27.0.

HomeBox is a home inventory and organization system. Prior to 0.27.0, a HomeBox password change revokes the user's other session tokens but does not revoke the user's API keys, and API keys have no default API-key expiration. An attacker who has obtained an API key can therefore retain full API-level access after the account owner changes the password and can keep that access indefinitely unless the owner discovers and manually deletes the key by ID. Because the password change terminates other sessions, the surviving API credential can evade the owner's expected containment and detection. This issue is fixed in version 0.27.0.

Chevereto before 4.5.8 contains a server-side request forgery vulnerability that allows authenticated administrators to cause the server to issue arbitrary requests by supplying a malicious URL to the uploadToWebsite function, which fetches the raw source via fetch_url before the Upload::checkValidUrl SSRF guard can be invoked. Attackers can target loopback addresses, RFC1918 internal services, cloud instance metadata endpoints, and file/gopher/dict schemes through the /json upload action to disclose internal responses or credentials when the fetched content is stored and served back as a public image URL.

CVSS 3.1 Base Score 9.3 (Confidentiality and Integrity impacts).  CVSS Vector: (CVSS:3.1/AV:N/AC:L/PR:N/UI:N/S:C/C:L/I:H/A:N).

Vulnerability in the Oracle Access Manager product of Oracle Fusion Middleware (component: Authentication Engine).  Supported versions that are affected are 12.2.1.4.0 and  14.1.2.1.0. Difficult to exploit vulnerability allows unauthenticated attacker with network access via SAML to compromise Oracle Access Manager.  While the vulnerability is in Oracle Access Manager, attacks may significantly impact additional products (scope change).  Successful attacks of this vulnerability can result in  unauthorized creation, deletion or modification access to critical data or all Oracle Access Manager accessible data as well as  unauthorized access to critical data or complete access to all Oracle Access Manager accessible data. CVSS 3.1 Base Score 8.7 (Confidentiality and Integrity impacts).  CVSS Vector: (CVSS:3.1/AV:N/AC:H/PR:N/UI:N/S:C/C:H/I:H/A:N).

Vulnerability in the Oracle Application Development Framework (ADF) product of Oracle Fusion Middleware (component: ADF Faces).   The supported version that is affected is 14.1.2.0.0. Easily exploitable vulnerability allows unauthenticated attacker with network access via HTTP to compromise Oracle Application Development Framework (ADF).  Successful attacks require human interaction from a person other than the attacker and while the vulnerability is in Oracle Application Development Framework (ADF), attacks may significantly impact additional products (scope change). Successful attacks of this vulnerability can result in  unauthorized update, insert or delete access to some of Oracle Application Development Framework (ADF) accessible data as well as  unauthorized read access to a subset of Oracle Application Development Framework (ADF) accessible data. CVSS 3.1 Base Score 6.1 (Confidentiality and Integrity impacts).  CVSS Vector: (CVSS:3.1/AV:N/AC:L/PR:N/UI:R/S:C/C:L/I:L/A:N).

Vulnerability in the Oracle Platform Security for Java product of Oracle Fusion Middleware (component: Centralized Thirdparty Jars).  Supported versions that are affected are 12.2.1.4.0 and  14.1.2.0.0. Easily exploitable vulnerability allows unauthenticated attacker with network access via HTTP to compromise Oracle Platform Security for Java.  While the vulnerability is in Oracle Platform Security for Java, attacks may significantly impact additional products (scope change).  Successful attacks of this vulnerability can result in  unauthorized access to critical data or complete access to all Oracle Platform Security for Java accessible data. CVSS 3.1 Base Score 8.6 (Confidentiality impacts).  CVSS Vector: (CVSS:3.1/AV:N/AC:L/PR:N/UI:N/S:C/C:H/I:N/A:N).

Vulnerability in the Service Delivery Platform product of Oracle Fusion Middleware (component: Messaging Enabler).  Supported versions that are affected are 12.2.1.4.0 and  14.1.2.0.0. Difficult to exploit vulnerability allows unauthenticated attacker with access to the physical communication segment attached to the hardware where the Service Delivery Platform executes to compromise Service Delivery Platform.  While the vulnerability is in Service Delivery Platform, attacks may significantly impact additional products (scope change).  Successful attacks of this vulnerability can result in takeover of Service Delivery Platform. CVSS 3.1 Base Score 8.3 (Confidentiality, Integrity and Availability impacts).  CVSS Vector: (CVSS:3.1/AV:A/AC:H/PR:N/UI:N/S:C/C:H/I:H/A:H).
Privilege escalation due to incorrect boundary conditions in the Graphics: CanvasWebGL component on Android. This vulnerability was fixed in Firefox 160.0.1.

Incorrect authorization in ASUS Control Center Express allows a remote authenticated user with a low-privileged role to create an administrator account, resulting in administrative control of the management console and of the clients it manages.
Refer to the '
Security Update for ASUS Control Center Express Agent  ' section on the ASUS Security Advisory for more information.

A path traversal flaw was found in ansible-core. When installing a collection with ansible-galaxy collection install, the install destination directory is derived from the namespace and name fields declared inside the collection artifact's own metadata, which are not validated as well-formed collection identifiers or checked for path containment. A malicious collection artifact -- delivered as a local file, a remote URL, a source directory, a git repository, or as a dependency -- can use a crafted name value to redirect the install destination outside the configured collections path, causing ansible-galaxy to delete an existing directory writable by the invoking user and then write attacker-controlled files to that location.

** UNSUPPORTED WHEN ASSIGNED ** 



Improper Authentication in Apache SeaTunnel Web 1.0.2 allows a user whose account has been disabled to authenticate with valid credentials and obtain a new login token. The login query does not check the account status, so disabling an account does not prevent new logins or access to protected APIs using the newly issued token. This issue requires valid credentials for the disabled account; it is not a credential-free authentication bypass.



Apache SeaTunnel Web is no longer maintained. The affected 1.0.2 release does not contain the account-status check added to the main branch in pull request #264. There is no maintained fixed release. Users should discontinue use of this unsupported component.



NOTE: This vulnerability only affects products that are no longer supported by the maintainer.

Insufficient Session Expiration vulnerability in the Apache Iggy server HTTP transport. A self-issued JSON Web Token (JWT) identified the user only by numeric user ID, and a new user takes the lowest free ID. After an administrator deleted a user, that user's unexpired token, or a token refreshed from it while the ID was free, authenticated as the next account created with that ID and had that account's permissions. Only deployments with HTTP enabled are affected.

This issue affects Apache Iggy: through 0.9.0.

Users are recommended to upgrade to version 0.10.0, which fixes the issue.

In Eclipse Mosquitto versions 2.0.0 to 2.0.22 and 2.1.0 to 2.1.2, the return value of password hash functions for sha512-pbkdf2 and legacy sha512 were not checked. Starting with OpenSSL 4.0, sha512-pbkdf2 hashing will fail when using the FIPS provider for passwords shorter than 8 characters. This has the effect that newly created passwords would match against any other password with fewer than 8 characters.

In the Apache Airflow Microsoft Azure provider 10.2.0 through 15.3.0, `S3ToAzureBlobStorageOperator` turned off TLS certificate verification for its connection to Amazon S3 by default (`s3_verify=False`), whatever the AWS connection's own verification settings were. An attacker positioned on the network between an Airflow worker and S3 could intercept that traffic, read the signed requests and alter the listed object keys and the copied file contents. Deployments are affected when a Dag uses `S3ToAzureBlobStorageOperator` without setting `s3_verify`. Users are advised to upgrade to apache-airflow-providers-microsoft-azure 15.3.1 or later, which uses the AWS connection's verification settings by default.

In Eclipse Mosquitto versions 2.1.0 to 2.1.2, a broker with a listener that is configured to use the PROXY protocol v2 is vulnerable to an untrusted proxy providing details that cause the broker to accept fake SSL information.



This can be mitigated by following the documented requirements for PROXY listeners: It is very important that only trusted proxies are allowed to connect to any listener using the PROXY protocol, and that clients are not allowed to connect to the listener at all.

In Eclipse versions 1.5-1.6.13, 2.0.0-2.0.22 and 2.1.0-2.1.2, the client library libmosquitto does not reject Will messages with payloads greater than 65535 bytes when calling `mosquitto_will_set()` or `mosquitto_will_set_v5()`. This results in up to 65535 bytes of uninitialised heap memory being transmitted as the Will.



This can be mitigated by only passing payloads with a maximum length of 65535 bytes.

Missing Authorization vulnerability in the Apache Iggy server. The system snapshot command (GetSnapshot on the binary transports and POST /snapshot on HTTP) checked only that the caller was logged in, not the read_servers or manage_servers permission. Any authenticated user, including a user with no permissions, could download a diagnostic archive with the server log files, the host process list, a file system listing and the runtime server configuration. The runtime configuration contains the HTTP JWT signing secret and the message encryption key when they are set in the configuration. If HTTP is enabled, the user could use the signing secret to create tokens for any account, including root.

This issue affects Apache Iggy: before 0.9.0.

Users are recommended to upgrade to version 0.10.0, which fixes the issue.

In Eclipse Mosquitto versions 2.1 through 2.1.2, a listener configured with `protocol websockets` mishandles empty WebSocket data frames. `net__read_ws()` in `lib/net_ws.c` returns the number of framing bytes consumed (the 4 masking-key bytes) for a data frame with a zero-length payload, without writing any bytes to the caller’s buffer. The MQTT packet reader in `packet__read_single()` (`lib/packet_mosq.c`) trusts that return value as a payload byte count. A remote client can therefore advance the read position over an uninitialised heap allocation, causing the broker to process and forward uninitialised heap memory (information disclosure, including heap and libc pointers), and can underflow the unsigned `to_process` counter so that subsequent attacker-controlled frame data is written past the end of the allocation (heap out-of-bounds write). The out-of-bounds write is reachable from the CONNECT packet before any authentication check, so an unauthenticated client can corrupt the heap and crash the broker even when `allow_anonymous false` is set. Combining the disclosure and the write allows remote code execution as the broker’s user by any client able to establish a session.
In Eclipse Mosquitto versions 2.1.0 to 2.1.2, the mosquitto_ctrl utility would crash if attempting to interact with a hostile broker and the broker sent a non-string "error" value.

In Eclipse Mosquitto versions 2.1.0 to 2.1.2, using the mosquitto_ctrl utility in interactive shell mode to interact with a malicious server could result in a crash of the utility if the server sent a hostile response.

The QUIC stack queues a RETIRE_CONNECTION_ID frame also for retransmitted NEW_CONNECTION_ID frames. This allows a remote malicious QUIC stack to queue an unlimited number of RETIRE_CONNECTION_ID frames.

Insertion of Sensitive Information into Log File vulnerability in the Apache Iggy server. If Apache Iggy 0.9.0 started without IGGY_ROOT_USERNAME and IGGY_ROOT_PASSWORD, it generated a root password and wrote it to the server log file, which is enabled by default. The system snapshot command (GetSnapshot on the binary transports and POST /snapshot on HTTP) let a user with only the read_servers permission download the server log files. That user could read the generated root password and log in as root.

This issue affects Apache Iggy: 0.9.0.

Users are recommended to upgrade to version 0.10.0, which fixes the issue. Version 0.10.0 never generates a root password, and the snapshot requires the manage_servers permission. If a 0.9.0 server generated its root password, change that password.
Calling EVP_EncodeBlock() with an input length close to INT_MAX may overflow the calculation of the encoded output size and write past the end of the caller-supplied output buffer.
Verifying a maliciously crafted CMS or PKCS#7 SignedData message with CRL checking enabled may consume excessive CPU time, growing with the square of the message size.

NocoDB before 2026.10.1 contains a stored CSS injection vulnerability that allows authenticated Commenter or Editor users to inject inline styles by placing single quotes in mention text. Attackers can break out of the single-quoted data-id attribute in comments or rich text cells to overlay or rearrange the interface for other viewers.

NocoDB before 2026.10.1 contains a stored HTML injection vulnerability that allows authenticated users with record edit rights to inject forms, images, and styled overlays into rich text cells, which are sanitized only with DOMPurify's default policy. Attackers can place a page-sized spoofed sign-in form or remote image in a cell to harvest passwords and disclose viewer IP addresses in expanded records, gallery and kanban cards, and shared views.

NocoDB before 2026.10.0 contains an sql injection vulnerability that allows authenticated users with the Creator role to inject SQL by supplying a crafted formula parsed_tree during table creation. Attackers can set a malicious binary-expression operator that is interpolated into a knex.raw fragment, reading user and token tables and escalating to super administrator on SQLite installs.

NocoDB before 2026.10.1 contains an incorrect authorization vulnerability that allows organization Creators to reach routes restricted to other roles because the aclFn middleware never enforced allowedRoles. Attackers can generate a super admin password reset link via org-users endpoints to take over the instance, or read and modify SSO client secrets.

NocoDB before 2026.10.1 contains an information disclosure vulnerability that allows unauthenticated attackers to download data exports by reconstructing predictable file paths under nc/uploads/data-export. Attackers can derive paths from the table id, base, table and view titles, and export time to read full exports, including fields hidden from public shared views.

NocoDB before 2026.10.1 contains a template injection vulnerability that allows authenticated Creator-role users to execute server-side JavaScript by supplying array-form property paths to Handlebars helpers in webhook templates. Attackers can bypass the string-only prototype guard to reach the function constructor, running operating-system commands with server privileges or exfiltrating process-internal values via outbound requests.

NocoDB from 0.253.0 before 2026.09.1 contains an incorrect authorization vulnerability in baseUserDelete that allows base Creators to remove higher-privileged Owners due to a broken role power comparison. Attackers holding the Creator role can remove other Owners of a base, since getProjectRolePower returns -1 for the target and never refuses the request.

NocoDB from 2026.07.0 before 2026.10.0 contains an sql injection vulnerability that allows users with Creator role to inject SQL through unescaped backslashes in the DATETIME_FORMAT formula format argument on MySQL-backed bases. Attackers can place a backslash before a quote to terminate the DATE_FORMAT string literal and read any data reachable by the data source's database user, including tables outside the base.

NocoDB before 2026.10.1 contains an authentication bypass vulnerability that allows holders of revoked OAuth access tokens to authenticate as first-party sessions by presenting them through the session header. Attackers can bypass revocation, client-existence, route allowlist and granted_resources scope checks to modify victim profiles, upload to storage, and force global sign-outs.

NocoDB before 2026.10.1 contains a credential exposure vulnerability in the connection-test endpoint that allows authorized integration users to redirect stored credentials by overriding connection host, port, and user fields. Attackers can point the test at a server they control to capture offline-crackable PostgreSQL md5 or MySQL handshakes and recover the stored database password.

NocoDB from 0.301.4 before 2026.10.0 contains an information disclosure vulnerability that allows authenticated workspace viewers to read pending invitation tokens through the workspace member list. Attackers can redeem an exposed higher-privileged invitation token at signup to claim the invited account and escalate to roles such as workspace owner.

NocoDB before 2026.10.1 contains a consent phishing vulnerability that allows unauthenticated attackers to register OAuth clients with arbitrary HTTPS redirect URIs through the unauthenticated dynamic client registration endpoint. Attackers can impersonate trusted applications on a consent screen lacking unverified-client warnings or redirect host display, obtaining tokens to read and write victim tables and records.

NocoDB before 2026.10.1 contains an SQL injection vulnerability because select-field option titles are embedded into MySQL or MariaDB enum/set column definitions with only single-quote doubling, leaving backslashes unescaped. A base creator or owner can end an option title with a backslash to escape the literal and append ALTER TABLE clauses, adding, dropping or renaming columns and altering indexes in the connected database.

NocoDB before 2026.10.0 contains an account takeover vulnerability that allows users with the base creator role to hijack other accounts by resending base invitations. Attackers can trigger baseUserInviteResend to mint a new invite_token, read it from the base member list, and reset the victim's password through signup, taking over owner or super admin accounts.

NocoDB before 2026.10.0 contains an information disclosure vulnerability that allows unauthenticated attackers to read hidden columns by supplying comma-separated group-by column lists. Attackers with a shared view link can pair a visible and hidden column to bypass restrictSharedViewColumnReferences and retrieve hidden values tied to individual rows.

NocoDB before 2026.10.0 contains an improper access control vulnerability that allows Creator-role users to attach NocoDB's internal database by supplying is_meta and is_local flags. Attackers can create sources or bases with these flags to expose user, token and integration tables, then read and modify records including user roles.

NocoDB before 2026.10.1 contains an information disclosure vulnerability that allows unauthenticated shared view link holders to read hidden columns by grouping on physical column names. Attackers can supply a hidden column's physical name or the unchecked sub-group parameter to the public group-by endpoint to reveal hidden values, counts, and column existence.

NocoDB before 2026.09.0 contains an sql injection vulnerability that allows authenticated Creator or Owner users to inject raw SQL by persisting a crafted formula parsed_tree reused without revalidation. Attackers can bypass the SQLite metadata path guard with an alias to plant the tree, escalating to super administrator or executing OS commands on external PostgreSQL hosts.

NocoDB from 0.301.4 before 2026.10.1 writes the nc_token session cookie from script in the Enterprise useGlobal composable without the Secure attribute. Network-positioned attackers can observe or induce plain-HTTP requests to https instances to capture the session token and impersonate the victim until expiry.

NocoDB before 2026.09.0 contains an improper authorization vulnerability that allows workspace Creator users to read plaintext notification webhook URLs by querying the webhook plugin listing endpoint. Attackers can replay exposed Slack, Teams, Discord and Mattermost webhook URLs directly against messaging providers to post arbitrary messages into organization chat channels.

NocoDB before 2026.09.0 contains a server-side template injection vulnerability that allows authenticated Creator or Owner users to execute JavaScript by abusing Handlebars webhook helpers. Attackers can supply property paths like constructor.constructor to pluck, sortBy, filter, or withSort helpers to reach the Function constructor and run operating-system commands.

NocoDB before 2026.09.0 contains a missing authorization vulnerability in the job status polling endpoint of jobs.controller.ts that lacks an @Acl decorator. Unauthenticated attackers with a job id can read buffered status messages and completion payloads, exposing signed export download URLs or new base identifiers.

NocoDB before 2026.09.0 contains an authorization bypass vulnerability in extract-ids.middleware.ts that allows authenticated users to resolve roles against another base by supplying an MCP token id in the query string. Attackers with Viewer access on one base can mint an MCP token and pass its id to read another base's metadata, including table lists and member email addresses.

NocoDB before 2026.08.1 contains an authorization bypass vulnerability that allows authenticated Creators to access another tenant's external database by reusing a victim source id when adding a source. Because NcConnectionMgrv2 caches connections by bare source id, attackers can reflect the victim's cached database schema and read, update, and insert records through their own base models.

NocoDB before 2026.10.1 contains a user enumeration vulnerability that allows unauthenticated attackers to identify pending invitees through a distinct sign-in error message. Attackers can submit sign-in requests where validateUser in auth.service.ts skips password comparison for saltless invited accounts, confirming the email address has an account.

NocoDB before 2026.10.1 contains a user enumeration vulnerability that allows unauthenticated attackers to determine registered email addresses by observing differing sign-up endpoint responses. Attackers can submit addresses to signup in users.service.ts and compare error messages to identify existing accounts and pending Enterprise invitations, even under invite-only signup.

NocoDB before 2026.08.0 contains an sql injection vulnerability that allows authenticated Creator or Owner users to execute database functions by supplying zero-argument function calls as column default values. Attackers can plant functions like version() or inet_server_addr() in PostgreSQL or MySQL column definitions and read results through record APIs, disclosing server addresses, role names, and engine details.

NocoDB before 2026.08.0 contains a stored cross-site scripting vulnerability that allows authenticated Creator or Editor users to execute script by injecting markup into fields rendered through URL() formulas. The canvas grid renderer assigns unsanitized formula output to innerHTML, letting attackers steal session tokens from localStorage and take over accounts of users viewing the table.

NocoDB before 2026.04.1 fails to clear reset_password_token and reset_password_expires in users.service.ts when a password is changed, leaving earlier reset links valid. Attackers holding an unexpired reset link, such as from prior mailbox access, can set a new password and regain control of the account.

NocoDB before 2026.08.0 contains an authorization bypass vulnerability that allows anonymous share link holders to access records excluded by a shared view's row filter, because the read-by-primary-key path ignores the view's filters. Attackers can request the public attachment-download or nested-link listing routes with a record id to mint signed download URLs for hidden files and read linked-record data.

NocoDB before 2026.08.0 contains an information disclosure vulnerability that allows unauthenticated shared-base link holders to read the base's stored plaintext password through the general base metadata endpoint. Attackers with a share link can query the base read or list responses in bases.controller.ts, which skip password stripping in sanitizeBase.ts, to obtain reusable plaintext passwords.

NocoDB before 2026.08.0 contains an insecure direct object reference vulnerability that allows unauthenticated attackers to access records hidden by a shared view's row filter by supplying arbitrary primary keys. Attackers with the share link can request attachment downloads and many-to-many or has-many link listings for excluded records to obtain their attachment files and linked record identities.

NocoDB from 2026.06.2 before 2026.08.0 contains an authorization bypass vulnerability that allows authenticated base Editors to write to data-read-only sources by abusing the internal batch endpoint. Attackers can name a writable decoy table on the batch envelope and target a read-only source table in dataUpdate, dataInsert or dataDelete sub-operations to modify or destroy records.

NocoDB before 2026.08.0 contains an authorization bypass in shared-view relation endpoints because parent-record lookups apply only the primary key, not the view's row filter. Anonymous share-link holders can enumerate auto-increment primary keys against the has-many, many-to-many, one-to-many and link-to-another-record routes to read linked records of filtered-out rows.

NocoDB before 2026.08.0 contains an information disclosure vulnerability that allows unauthenticated attackers to access attachments of filtered-out records through the shared view attachment-download endpoint. Attackers holding a public share link can enumerate sequential primary keys to obtain signed download paths for files on records the view's row filter excludes.

NocoDB before 2026.08.0 contains a server-side request forgery vulnerability that allows authenticated base Editors to make backend HTTP requests by supplying arbitrary URLs to the integration remote fetch operation. Attackers can control the method, headers, and body to reach internal APIs, loopback services, and cloud metadata endpoints, reading responses and echoed decrypted integration secrets.

NocoDB before 2026.10.0 contains an insecure direct object reference vulnerability that allows authenticated users to obtain signed download URLs for other bases' attachments by storing foreign attachment paths in their own rows via prepareNocoData. Attackers with write access to an attachment column can have _convertAttachmentType or the attachment download endpoint sign the foreign path, reading cross-base files despite secure attachment mode.

NocoDB before 2026.07.0 contains an SQL injection vulnerability in its MySQL and SQLite clients that inserts the column precision value into generated data-definition statements without numeric validation. Authenticated users with the Creator or Owner base role can supply a crafted precision value when creating or updating a column to close the type declaration and execute arbitrary SQL against the base's data source.

NocoDB before 2026.08.0 contains an authorization bypass vulnerability in public shared-view endpoints that fetch records by primary key without applying the view's row filter. Anonymous share link holders can enumerate sequential primary keys on link, has-many, and attachment download endpoints to read excluded records' linked data and download their attachments.

NocoDB before 2026.08.0 contains a stored cross-site scripting vulnerability that allows any authenticated user to register OAuth clients with javascript: redirect URIs. Attackers can send a consent link to a signed-in victim so either consent button runs script in the NocoDB origin, stealing the session token for account takeover.

NocoDB before 2026.08.0 contains an authorization bypass in its public shared-view relation endpoints, which verify that a parent record exists but not that it passes the view's row filters. Unauthenticated attackers holding a public share link can supply guessable auto-incrementing ids of filtered-out records to has-many, many-to-many, one-many, or link endpoints to read their child records.

NocoDB before 2026.10.1 contains an authentication bypass vulnerability that allows OAuth token holders to act as full sessions because OAuth access tokens are signed with the instance JWT secret. Attackers can present a narrowly scoped OAuth token to the session strategy, short-lived-token exchange, or NocoSocket handshake to gain the granting user's full privileges.

NocoDB before 2026.05.3 contains an account takeover vulnerability that allows invited users to complete other invitees' signups because batch invitations share one token across all recipients. Attackers holding a valid batch invite can submit another invitee's email with the shared non-expiring token to set its password and take over that account, including higher-role ones.

Insufficient Session Expiration vulnerability in the Apache Iggy Go SDK. The TCP client method CreatePersonalAccessToken wrote the 32-bit expiry into the upper half of the 64-bit expiry field that the server reads. The server read a nonzero expiry as 2^32 times the requested value. A token created through the Go TCP client therefore stayed valid about four billion times longer than the caller asked for.

This issue affects Apache Iggy Go SDK: from 0.5.0 before 0.10.0.

Users are recommended to upgrade to version 0.10.0, which fixes the issue. Tokens that an earlier version created keep their long expiry on the server. Delete those tokens and create new ones.
A DANE-enabled TLS client may crash by dereferencing a NULL pointer when processing an unusual combination of certificate and TLSA records.

Supergateway 2.4.0 through 4.2.2 contains a cross-site WebSocket hijacking vulnerability in stdio-to-WebSocket mode that allows malicious web pages to connect by bypassing missing Origin header validation. Attackers can open the /message WebSocket from a victim's browser, even against localhost-bound gateways, to initialize an MCP session and invoke wrapped stdio MCP server tools with victim privileges.

WarehousePG (WHPG) 6.27.1 through 6.27.7 and 7.2.1 through 7.6.1 are affected by an out-of-bounds write vulnerability (CWE-787) in gpfdist, the file server used to load and unload external tables. When gpfdist attaches a request to a session, it sizes two internal arrays from the client-supplied X-GP-SEGMENT-COUNT header and writes to them at the index given by the X-GP-SEGMENT-ID header, without checking that the index is non-negative and smaller than the count (CWE-129). gpfdist does not authenticate callers unless gpfdists is used with client certificate verification, so an attacker who can reach the gpfdist port can crash it with a single HTTP request, failing every external table load or unload that uses that gpfdist instance. gpfdist is normally reachable only from the cluster's internal network.

In Eclipse Mosquitto versions 1.6 to 2.0.22 and 2.1.0 to 2.1.2, an MQTT v5.0 client connecting with a will-delay-interval that subsequently disconnects with a shorter interval causes all delayed wills to be suppressed.

A flaw was found in cyrus-sasl. When processing authentication requests using the Salted Challenge Response Authentication Mechanism (SCRAM), a remote attacker can trigger a null pointer dereference by submitting unexpected channel-binding data. This causes the server process to crash before validating authentication proofs, leading to a Denial of Service (DoS).
Dell PowerStore contains a CSV Injection vulnerability. A high-privileged attacker could exploit this vulnerability, potentially leading to code execution on another user's workstation.

openSIS 5.1 before 9.0 contains a local file inclusion vulnerability that allows authenticated users to include arbitrary files through the modname parameter of ajax.php. Attackers can prefix a payload with misc/ and use ../ directory traversal to read sensitive files like /etc/passwd or execute local scripts in the web server context. Exploitation evidence was first observed by the Shadowserver Foundation on 2023-10-19.

Baidu UEditor 1.4.0 through 1.4.3.3 contains an unrestricted file upload vulnerability in the catchimage action of /ueditor/net/controller.ashx that only validates the Content-Type header. Unauthenticated attackers can supply a source[] URL like x.jpg?.aspx to retain a malicious extension and write an executable .aspx file for remote code execution. Exploitation evidence was first observed by the Shadowserver Foundation on 2023-10-17.

FineReport 8.0 contains a path traversal vulnerability that allows unauthenticated attackers to read arbitrary files through the resourcepath parameter of the /WebReport/ReportServer endpoint. Attackers can send GET requests with op=chart and cmd=get_geo_json to read sensitive files like privilege.xml and extract admin credentials. Exploitation evidence was first observed by the Shadowserver Foundation on 2023-10-19.

Rocket.Chat versions 0.61.0 before 3.11.4, 3.12.x before 3.12.4 and 3.13.x before 3.13.2 contain a missing authorization vulnerability allowing unauthenticated attackers to read any room's messages via the livechat:loadHistory Meteor method. Attackers can mint a guest token through livechat:registerGuest and send POST requests to /api/v1/method.callAnon with a target rid parameter to retrieve message history without membership checks. Exploitation evidence was first observed by the Shadowserver Foundation on 2025-02-13.

OTOBO 10.0.1 before 10.0.13 contains an open redirect vulnerability that allows unauthenticated attackers to redirect users by supplying arbitrary URLs to the ExternalURLJump action. Attackers can craft GET requests to /otobo/index.pl?Action=ExternalURLJump with a malicious URL parameter, which the ExternalURLJump.pm module redirects to without an allow-list check, enabling phishing attacks. Exploitation evidence was first observed by the Shadowserver Foundation on 2023-10-23.

Synway SMG Gateway Management Software builds through 2022-03-15 contain a path traversal vulnerability that allows unauthenticated attackers to read arbitrary files via the downfile parameter in /down.php. Attackers can send a multipart POST request to /down.php with a traversal path in downfile to retrieve sensitive files like /etc/passwd. Exploitation evidence was first observed by the Shadowserver Foundation on 2023-10-20.

JoomBri Careers 3.3.0 contains a reflected cross-site scripting vulnerability that allows unauthenticated attackers to inject scripts through the 'keyword' parameter of the /for-jobseekers/search-jobs endpoint in com_jbcareers. Attackers can craft malicious URLs using an attribute-breakout payload with onfocus and autofocus to execute arbitrary JavaScript and steal session tokens or credentials. Exploitation evidence was first observed by the Shadowserver Foundation on 2023-10-23.

Nuxt 3.0.0 before 3.4.2 contains a semi-arbitrary file read vulnerability in the vite-node dev server middleware that allows unauthenticated attackers to read files by supplying an absolute path as the moduleId. Attackers can send GET requests to /__nuxt_vite_node__/module/ with an absolute file path to read sensitive system files. Exploitation evidence was first observed by the Shadowserver Foundation on 2023-10-19.

Bagisto 2.1.0 before 2.2.1 contains a client-side template injection vulnerability in the search page where the 'query' parameter is rendered unescaped inside a Vue app root. Unauthenticated attackers can send crafted VueJS template expressions to the /bagisto-common/search endpoint via the 'query' parameter to execute arbitrary JavaScript in victims' browsers. Exploitation evidence was first observed by the Shadowserver Foundation on 2024-07-30.

When NGINX Plus or NGINX Open Source is configured as a mail proxy, undisclosed traffic can cause a use-after-free in an nginx worker process. Additionally, attackers can execute code on systems with Address Space Layout Randomization (ASLR) disabled or when the attacker can bypass ASLR.

Impact:
A remote unauthenticated attacker may crash an nginx worker process or corrupt its memory, disrupting service. Remote code execution is a potential impact. There is no control plane exposure; this is a data plane issue only.



Note: Software versions which have reached End of Technical Support (EoTS) are not evaluated.

When using the listen directive with the ssl parameter in the http block with TLSv1.3 enabled, an attacker can use a specially crafted TLS connection to cause an infinite loop in the NGINX worker process while reading the HTTP request body. As a result, the worker process stops accepting new connections and processing existing connections. Note: Software versions which have reached End of Technical Support (EoTS) are not evaluated.

Impact: This vulnerability allows a remote, unauthenticated attacker to cause a denial-of-service (DoS) of NGINX. There is no control plane exposure; this is a data plane issue only.



Note: Software versions which have reached End of Technical Support (EoTS) are not evaluated.

Description:
This issue affects NGINX Plus and NGINX Open Source configurations that use HTTP/3. A remote, unauthenticated attacker can cause a use-after-free condition in the NGINX worker process, leading to a restart. Exploitation also depends on conditions beyond the attacker’s control. Additionally, attackers can execute code on systems with Address Space Layout Randomization (ASLR) disabled or when the attacker can bypass ASLR.

Impact:
This vulnerability may allow remote attackers to cause a denial-of-service (DoS) on the NGINX system or to possibly trigger a code execution. There is no control plane exposure; this is a data plane issue only.



Note: Software versions which have reached End of Technical Support (EoTS) are not evaluated.

This issue affects NGINX Plus or NGINX Open Source configurations that use HTTP/2. When NGINX processes undisclosed traffic, the flow control window can exceed the allowed threshold, potentially resulting in a heap buffer overflow typically followed by an NGINX worker segmentation fault. Additionally, attackers can execute code on systems with Address Space Layout Randomization (ASLR) disabled or when the attacker can bypass ASLR.

Impact: An attacker could leverage this vulnerability to crash the NGINX worker process, corrupt its memory, or potentially execute code remotely. There is no control plane exposure; this is a data plane issue only.



Note: Software versions which have reached End of Technical Support (EoTS) are not evaluated.

When NGINX Plus or NGINX Open Source is configured to use HTTP/2 for client connections and proxy client requests to a backend, a specially crafted request can result in use-after-free in the worker process, if this process is running low on worker_connections. Additionally, attackers can execute code on systems with Address Space Layout Randomization (ASLR) disabled or when the attacker can bypass ASLR.




Impact:



This vulnerability may allow remote attackers to cause a denial-of-service (DoS) on the NGINX system or may allow a code execution. There is no control plane exposure; this is a data plane issue only.



Note: Software versions which have reached End of Technical Support (EoTS) are not evaluated.

This issue occurs when NGINX Plus or NGINX Open Source is configured as a proxy, the proxied server name includes variables, and a Server Side Includes (SSI) or mirror directive sends a subrequest to a location that resolves the same server name. Under these conditions, a specially crafted HTTP request may cause a use-after-free condition in a worker process. An attacker may also be able to execute code if Address Space Layout Randomization (ASLR) is disabled or the attacker can bypass ASLR.

Impact: 
An attacker could leverage this vulnerability to crash the NGINX worker process, corrupt its memory, or perform remote code execution (RCE)



Note: Software versions which have reached End of Technical Support (EoTS) are not evaluated.

Description
When NGINX Plus or NGINX Open Source is configured with the ngx_stream_ssl_preread_module module, a specially crafted ClientHello message from an unauthenticated attacker causes forged values of the ngx_stream_ssl_preread_module variables, affecting virtual server selection. In addition, it may also cause a disagreement with a proxied server terminating the SSL/TLS connection without Transport Layer Security (TLS) 1.3 support.

Impact
This vulnerability may allow an attacker to forge values of the ngx_stream_ssl_preread_module variables and bypass the NGINX systems stream routing segmentation. As a result, the attacker may be able to route the connection to a privileged or internal backend that should be unreachable and gain access to sensitive information. There is no control plane exposure; this is a data plane issue only.






Note: Software versions which have reached End of Technical Support (EoTS) are not evaluated.

When NGINX Plus or NGINX Open Source is configured to use the try_files and alias directives with a map variable, certain combinations of regular expression captures in map and try_files can cause a segmentation fault in an NGINX worker process.

Impact:
An attacker could leverage this vulnerability to cause an NGINX worker process to terminate unexpectedly. There is no control plane exposure; this is a data plane issue only.



Note: Software versions which have reached End of Technical Support (EoTS) are not evaluated.

Dagu 1.23.0 before 2.0.0 defaults auth.mode to none, allowing unauthenticated attackers to execute OS commands through the /api/v2/dag-runs endpoint. Attackers can send a POST request with an inline spec defining steps containing arbitrary shell commands to achieve remote code execution. Exploitation evidence was first observed by the Shadowserver Foundation on 2026-03-11.

PHPGurukul Beauty Parlour Management System V1.1 uses a non-cryptographic function to generate security-sensitive appointment and invoice identifiers. The identifiers are generated within a restricted numeric range and are subsequently used in record lookup operations. This implementation exposes the application to identifier prediction or guessing attacks under conditions where the identifiers are relied upon as a security boundary.

Fleet before 4.92.0 contains a CSV formula injection vulnerability in the host inventory export endpoint that allows attackers controlling an enrolled host or enroll secret to plant spreadsheet formulas. Attackers can set osquery-reported fields like hostname or hardware serial to formula values, enabling data exfiltration or DDE command execution when users open the exported CSV.

Chamilo LMS is an open-source learning management system. Prior to 1.11.40 and 2.0.1, main/lp/lp_ajax_save_objectives.php and public/main/lp/lp_ajax_save_objectives.php trust the request uid parameter instead of the authenticated user identity when saving SCORM learning objectives. Any authenticated student can replace uid with another user's identifier and overwrite that user's objectives because the endpoint performs no ownership check. This issue is fixed in versions 1.11.40 and 2.0.1.

Chamilo LMS is an open-source learning management system. Prior to 2.0.3, public/main/course_description/course_description_controller.php assigns contentDescription directly from a teacher's request in the Doctrine-based add and edit paths without cross-site scripting sanitization. The stored value is rendered by src/CoreBundle/Resources/views/Course/about.html.twig through description with raw output, and the /course/{id}/about route is publicly accessible. A teacher can store active content that executes when an authenticated or unauthenticated visitor views the course description, enabling session theft, credential phishing, defacement, or actions in an authenticated victim's session. This issue is fixed in version 2.0.3.

Chamilo LMS is an open-source learning management system. Prior to 1.11.40 and 2.0.3, main/lp/scormItem.class.php and public/main/lp/scormItem.class.php store an attacker-controlled title element from imsmanifest.xml without cross-site scripting sanitization when a teacher imports a SCORM package. The title reaches c_lp_item.title and is rendered by src/CoreBundle/Resources/views/LearnPath/scorm_list.html.twig through item.title with raw output while Twig auto-escaping is disabled; the default configuration does not apply the optional AI-disclosure sanitization path. Enrolled students or administrators who view the learning-path table of contents can execute the stored content in their browser sessions. This issue is fixed in versions 1.11.40 and 2.0.3.

Chamilo LMS is an open-source learning management system. Prior to 2.0.3, POST /api/social_posts accepts attacker-controlled content that SocialPost::setContent stores without cross-site scripting sanitization, and assets/vue/components/social/SocialWallPost.vue renders post.content through v-html without sanitization. Any authenticated user can create a social-wall post that executes active content when another authenticated user views the wall. The script can run in an administrator's browser session and expose session data or perform actions with the victim's privileges. This issue is fixed in version 2.0.3.

Chamilo LMS is an open-source learning management system. From 2.0.0 until 2.0.3, the BigBlueButton plugin is vulnerable to XML External Entity (XXE) injection when an authenticated administrator configures a malicious BigBlueButton server URL. Processing attacker-controlled XML from that server can read arbitrary local files and perform Server-Side Request Forgery (SSRF). Sensitive configuration, credentials, source code, and internal network resources may be exposed. This issue is fixed in version 2.0.3.

Chamilo LMS is an open-source learning management system. Prior to 1.11.40 and 2.0.3, src/Chamilo/CourseBundle/Component/CourseCopy/CourseRestorer.php and src/CourseBundle/Component/CourseCopy/CourseRestorer.php use paths supplied by an imported legacy course backup without consistently confining them to the extraction directory. A course teacher can import a crafted backup containing parent-directory path segments, causing file operations to write attacker-controlled content outside the intended destination, including PHP-executable or automatically loaded locations. This can result in code execution as the PHP process and compromise course data, user data, credentials, and the host. This issue is fixed in versions 1.11.40 and 2.0.3.

Chamilo LMS is an open-source learning management system. Prior to 1.11.40 on the 1.11 release line and in 2.0.0, plugin/cleandeletedfiles/src/ajax.php and public/plugin/CleanDeletedFiles/src/ajax.php pass the request path parameter and list parameter directly to unlink without canonicalization, filename validation, or confinement to the plugin's scanned directories. An authenticated administrator can delete arbitrary files writable by the web server; a cross-site request forgery against an administrator session can reach the same operation. Deleting application source, uploaded content, cache, or configuration files can cause data loss and denial of service. This issue is fixed in version 1.11.40 on the 1.11 release line. No fixed 2.0 release is established as of this review.

Chamilo LMS is an open-source learning management system. Prior to 1.11.40, main/inc/ajax/user_manager.ajax.php exposes the update_users action without an authorization check and stores attacker-controlled firstname, lastname, and email values without HTML sanitization. An unauthenticated attacker can modify another user's profile fields, and the stored content executes when user_portal.php, the administrative user listing, user information, social profile, course participant list, or message-composer recipient header renders the modified account. Targeting an administrator account can expose administrator-session data or permit actions in that session. This issue is fixed in version 1.11.40.

Chamilo LMS is an open-source learning management system. Prior to 1.11.40, main/dropbox/dropbox_functions.inc.php accepts a literal .htaccess filename in the course dropbox and stores it in a directory served by Apache, where the file can alter handler behavior under the required AllowOverride All configuration. Any authenticated course participant can upload .htaccess and then upload a PHP payload disguised as a .gif, resulting in code execution as the web-server user when the dropbox tool is enabled. This can expose or modify the Chamilo installation, course content, and database credentials. This issue is fixed in version 1.11.40.

Chamilo LMS is an open-source learning management system. Prior to 1.11.40, main/inc/ajax/record_audio_rtc.ajax.php concatenates the user-controlled audio_dir parameter with the course document root and passes the result to recursive directory creation without path normalization. An authenticated course user can select directory paths outside the intended course storage tree wherever the web-server account has permission to create directories. The resulting filesystem changes can interfere with application layout or support a separate file-write or code-execution chain, although this endpoint alone is not shown to write attacker-selected file content outside the course tree. This issue is fixed in version 1.11.40.
